title: Principality of Liechtenstein
capsule: The Principality of Liechtenstein was constituted in 1719 when Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI combined the lordship of Schellenberg and the county of Vaduz into an imperial principality for Hans Adam I of Liechtenstein, a title obtained primarily for the political benefit of a seat in the Imperial Diet. The principality joined the Confederation of the Rhine in 1806, which dissolved its remaining feudal obligations to the Habsburg emperor and gave it de facto sovereignty; it was formally confirmed in the German Confederation in 1815. Throughout this period the Liechtenstein princes rarely visited their small Alpine holding, governing it instead through appointed stewards.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well established; Liechtenstein's boundaries have been stable since 1719 and are documented in imperial and later German Confederation records.
